panels.title: Objects synced
panels.description: Objects successfully copied to the destination, per second. Scoped by the bucket filter above.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Bytes written to the destination, per second.

panels.title: Objects failing
panels.description: Object transfers that ended in an error, per second. Anything above zero is worth opening the per-bucket table below.

panels.title: Cycle failures (1 h)
panels.description: Whole watch cycles that failed and were retried with backoff, over the last hour. A cycle fails when discovery or transfer returns a non-permanent error; tranquila keeps running and retries.

panels.title: Endpoint pacing
panels.description: 1 while congestion control has reduced an endpoint's rate limit below its configured base. Always 'Normal' when --source-rate-limit is 0 (the default), because AIMD is inert without a finite limit to halve.

panels.title: Active transfer workers
panels.description: Workers currently executing a transfer, out of --workers. Pinned at the maximum means the pool is the bottleneck; sitting at zero while objects are pending means discovery is not feeding it.

panels.title: Object outcomes per second
panels.description: Successful versus failed object transfers. Both are rates over the same window, so they are directly comparable on one axis.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Bytes per second written to the destination, summed over the selected buckets.

panels.title: Mean transfer duration per bucket
panels.description: rate(sum)/rate(count) of the transfer-duration histogram — an exact mean, not a quantile estimate. Bucket names are an open set, so series colors are hashed from the name: a bucket keeps its color when other buckets are filtered out. The y axis is logarithmic so buckets an order of magnitude apart stay readable together.

targets.expr: sum by (bucket) (rate(tranquila_transfer_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", bucket=~"$bucket"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (bucket) (rate(tranquila_transfer_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", bucket=~"$bucket"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: S3 errors by class
panels.description: Failed S3 calls by how tranquila classified them. 'transient' drives retry and congestion control, 'throttle' halves the rate limit immediately, 'permanent' is the only class that can terminate a cycle — and only when every failure in that cycle is permanent.

panels.title: Mean S3 call duration by operation
panels.description: rate(sum)/rate(count) per operation — an exact mean. Deliberately not a p95: the histogram's largest finite bucket is 10 s, so any quantile above that is extrapolated and unreliable. Use the panel below for the slow tail. The y axis is logarithmic: list calls and object calls differ by three orders of magnitude, and a linear axis flattens every fast operation onto the baseline.

panels.title: S3 calls slower than 10 s
panels.description: Calls per second landing above the histogram's largest finite bucket (le=10000ms), computed as count minus that bucket. Exact, unlike a quantile in the same range. The le matcher is a regex because Prometheus 3 normalises bucket bounds to 10000.0 while Prometheus 2 keeps 10000 — an exact match silently returns no data on one of them. Sustained ListObjectsV2 here is the signature of discovery that cannot finish: list attempts get a 60 s deadline that escalates to 240 s.

panels.title: Effective S3 rate limit
panels.description: Current calls-per-second ceiling per endpoint, after congestion control. 0 means unlimited (--source-rate-limit=0, the default) — in that state the line sits flat at zero and AIMD never engages.

panels.title: Rate-limit adjustments
panels.description: Congestion-control decisions per second. 'decrease' is AIMD halving after repeated transient failures or one throttle; 'increase' is additive recovery.

panels.title: Per-bucket sync detail
panels.description: The same numbers as the charts above, per bucket, as text. Sort any column. This is the table view for the whole dashboard; every individual panel also has one under its menu → Inspect → Data.

targets.expr: sum by (bucket) (rate(tranquila_transfer_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", bucket=~"$bucket"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (bucket) (rate(tranquila_transfer_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", bucket=~"$bucket"}[$__rate_interval]))

options.content:
### What this dashboard can and cannot tell you

These limits are properties of the metrics tranquila currently emits, not of the
queries. They are written here so a panel is never read as saying more than it can.

**S3 call latency tops out at 10 s.** `tranquila.s3.operation.duration` uses the
OpenTelemetry default bucket boundaries, whose largest finite bucket is 10 000 ms.
Every list attempt slower than that — which is the interesting case, since the
per-attempt deadline starts at 60 s and escalates to 240 s — falls into one bucket.
A `histogram_quantile` above 10 s would be extrapolation, so no panel here shows one.
*Mean S3 call duration* is exact; *S3 calls slower than 10 s* is exact; a p95 would not be.

**S3 latency and errors cannot be split by endpoint.**
`tranquila.s3.operation.duration` carries `operation`, `bucket` and `status`, but no
`endpoint` label, so source and destination call latency are pooled. Only
`tranquila.s3.errors`, `tranquila.s3.rate_limit` and `tranquila.s3.rate_limit.changes`
are per-endpoint.

**There are no discovery metrics.** Nothing reports prefixes walked, pages listed,
checkpoints saved or resumed, or a prefix parked on an unanswerable page. A bucket
stuck in discovery shows up here only indirectly: `ListObjectsV2` appearing in
*S3 calls slower than 10 s*, transient errors climbing, and that bucket contributing
nothing in *Per-bucket sync detail*. The logs remain the only direct source.

**Queue depth is not exported.** `tranquila.workers.active` shows how many workers are
busy, not how many objects are waiting, so saturation is visible but backlog is not.

**Endpoint pacing reads 'Normal' when rate limiting is off.** With
`--source-rate-limit=0` (the default) the limiter is `rate.Inf` and congestion control
returns early, so *Effective S3 rate limit* sits at 0 and *Endpoint pacing* can never
leave Normal. That is the configured state, not a healthy one.
